newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong gold ends shade down on Aussie sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends shade down on Aussie sales.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended down from New York's previous close after the price remained practically stagnant, balanced between buy-backs and sales from Australian producers in intraday trade.
Bullion ended at US$323.50/324.00 on Friday compared to New York's previous close at US$$324.00/50 on Thursday.
"The market traded at around $323.50 per ounce almost the whole day," said one dealer.
Hong Kong gold opened slighty lower from New York's close and closed unchanged from its open.
Traders reported shortcovering and buy-backs from Australian producers, and others noted Australian selling.
Physical demand would perk up slightly below $320 per ounce, dealers said.
The market was seen trending lower and sentiment was bearish and expected to remain so over the next week.
Local tael gold ended HK$22 up at HK$2,996 per tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -5.00 from its previous fix at -6.00.
